subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 07, 2026
body:
The AcreetionOS continuous integration pipeline has just seen another round of enhancements, building on the recent introduction of per-pipeline staging directories and relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, which has significantly improved the reliability of our ISO build process. This ongoing refinement is a testament to our community's dedication to delivering a stable and seamless experience for users.

Development
The recent updates to our CI pipeline have been focused on avoiding publish races between concurrent builds, and you can track these changes on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html. Our team has been working tirelessly to ensure that our distribution meets the highest standards of quality, and we're excited to see the impact of these improvements on our users. For more information on our development process and how to get involved, you can visit our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html.

Community
We've also seen some exciting developments in the broader Linux ecosystem, including the release of Emacs 31.1 and the latest stable kernel set, which includes versions 7.1.10 and 6.18.46. Our community has been actively engaged in discussing these updates and how they can be leveraged to improve AcreetionOS. If you're interested in learning more about our community and how to participate, you can visit our documentation page at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html. Additionally, you can check out our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html for the latest news and updates on AcreetionOS. 

Tip of the day
As we continue to refine our distribution, we encourage users to explore our documentation and wiki pages to learn more about AcreetionOS and how to get the most out of it. Whether you're a seasoned Linux user or just starting out, our community is always here to help, and you can find more information about our project at https://acreetionos.org/.
